_note: Each task run once through Harbor 0.25.0 with the built-in terminus-2 agent (`python -m alegen.modelrun`, see its docstring for what differs from a plain `harbor run` on this host: locally built images, no network in the container during the agent phase, model calls made by the Harbor process through a local streaming shim). Task content and time limits unchanged; `max_turns=150`. Ten tasks: the hardest level of every family (seven level-4 tasks, and the level-3 task for amplicon_16s, md_system_repair and somatic_tn). The agent is text-only: it cannot look at screenshots. Tokens are the sums over all turns as reported by the provider (the agent resends the whole history every turn, so most input tokens are cache hits). Models reached through OpenRouter are pinned to one named provider per model (OpenRouter serves most of these models from many providers, often with quantised weights). `cost estimate` is what LiteLLM computes from its price table, not the amount billed: for kimi-k3 the table has a price for cached input, so the estimate should be close to the bill; for gemini-3.8-flash it has none, so cached input is counted at the full input price and the figure is an upper bound.

level5.note: Level 5: the authored task without stated acceptance criteria, verification procedures and audit checklist. Level 6: also without the sentences that tell the reader what to look out for (incident reports and the like), so that the evidence is only in the data and the file metadata. Both are text-only transformations (alegen/descaffold.py): inputs other than the edited notes, and the hidden reference, are byte-identical to the authored level (level 4; level 3 for amplicon_16s). Level 7: a new silent decision point in the data (family author), with the level-6 text. Where the level-5/6 scorer has one component less (audit or mapping deliverable removed), the output each model produced on the authored level was scored again with it (alegen.rescore) to compare like with like. One attempt per cell: reward (wall time, agent turns; lowest component if not 1). `-` = that level does not exist for the family.

project.note: Three independent level-4 instances of crispr_screen (seeds 1-3) in one task; accepted only if every part is (alegen/project.py). The first part is the single task of the left column. Run with max_turns=450 and a 3-hour limit.

g8.note: Gate G8 (alegen/g8.py): an instance that passed G1-G7 is kept as hard only if the yardstick model fails every one of at least two attempts; `drop` = it passed every attempt, `unstable` = mixed, `pending` = fewer than two attempts. The first attempt of a task is the one in the tables above.
